# Daily declaration synchronization

This is a proposed architecture. No application code or schema has changed.

The recommendation is incremental acquisition with complete-snapshot interpretation. Discover changed members, reacquire their complete declaration histories, merge retained raw evidence, then run global cleaning, resolution, and atomic loading. Keep the first implementation compatible with existing resolution semantics. Fully incremental resolution is a separate investment.

## Options

| Approach | Acquisition | Interpretation and publication | Main tradeoff |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Full acquisition with content diff | Every stored member | Rebuild when evidence changes | Smallest departure, no remote acquisition saving |
| Changed-member acquisition with complete snapshot | Full histories of affected members | Complete corpus | Recommended first version. Reuses member partitions and retains global context |
| Changed-interest acquisition with complete snapshot | Unfiltered records for discovered IDs | Complete corpus | Less acquisition, more relationship, ownership, and record-merge handling |
| Fully incremental processing | Changed records | Affected dependencies and identity components | Requires durable evidence, identity merge/split rules, reverse dependencies, and global alias maintenance |

No runtime or cost reduction has been measured. Complete resolution and grouping remain global work.

## Proposed caller experience

```sh
exposed data declarations sync --config CONFIG
exposed data declarations sync --config CONFIG --reconcile
exposed data declarations sync --config CONFIG --resume RUN_ID
```

Daily sync bootstraps a complete capture if there is no committed base. Reconciliation scans the retained member cohort again. Resume continues a sealed run without changing its evidence under the same run ID. Existing stage commands remain replay and inspection tools. They cannot bypass generation validation when publishing to the synchronized projection.

## Acquisition and snapshot

Read the committed generation and discovery checkpoint from Postgres. Freeze an inclusive date window with configurable overlap and indexing lag. The source exposes dates, so the boundary must define its calendar policy explicitly. Query publication and update windows separately, then union their results. Registration dates are not correction timestamps.

Filtered responses identify changed members. Fetch their complete histories without date filters, with expired records included and children separate. Add newly stored members even when discovery is empty. Unknown discovered members must be loaded and fully backfilled, or fail the run visibly; never silently skip them. Preserve former members already in the retained scope.

Observed API behavior makes hydration necessary. For interest 14513, an update-filtered list returned register 822 only. The same list endpoint filtered solely by InterestIds returned registers 822 and 794. The filtered response therefore cannot replace complete raw evidence. Probe responses are retained beside this document. This observation does not prove the behavior of every API query.

Merge reacquired records into immutable member partitions keyed by DeclarationId, checking member ownership. Retain old records missing from a response as discrepancies until withdrawal semantics are established. Snapshot manifests reference all member partitions, including reused immutable files. Record hashes, query policy, cohort, capture times, discovery receipts, and expected base generation. Materialize the complete snapshot for current stage readers. Do not relabel old evidence as freshly fetched. Compare canonical content separately from retrieval timestamps.

Only seal a capture after every planned member and page completes. Stage files under unique names and publish after closing and verifying them. Reject HTTP errors, inconsistent pagination, duplicate conflicting records, and truncated responses. Use bounded retries. Offset pagination has no documented transactional snapshot guarantee; overlap and periodic reconciliation reduce this risk but do not prove losslessness.

## Interpretation and publication

Run existing global clean and resolve over the complete merged snapshot. This retains parent evidence, reconsiders children whose parents changed, and derives company aliases from all surviving observations. Publish the complete resolved projection, because changed identity components can affect declarations outside the source delta.

Prepare durable immutable artifacts before the database transaction. Inside the existing declaration-loader lock, check the expected base generation, load the projection, rebuild groups, record the snapshot reference and fingerprints, and advance the discovery checkpoint in one transaction. An already committed run returns its recorded result before checking its old base. A stale base rejects publication and requires rebuilding against the current generation.

A crash before commit leaves the old checkpoint and projection. Resume can reuse sealed artifacts. A crash after commit returns the committed result. A successful empty scan advances coverage without replacing evidence or changing funder identities. Artifact retention pins every partition referenced by the committed snapshot. Production storage must survive scheduler replacement; the database projection cannot reconstruct complete source evidence.

## Domain ownership and sketch

```rust
enum SyncMode { Daily, Reconcile }
struct DiscoveryWindow { /* checked inclusive source dates */ }
struct PublishedGeneration { /* generation, snapshot reference, coverage */ }
struct CompleteCapture { /* privately constructed from verified traversal */ }
struct PreparedPublication { /* expected base, run, snapshot, load fingerprint */ }
enum PublishOutcome { Committed(SyncReport), AlreadyCommitted(SyncReport), StaleBase }

impl DeclarationSyncService {
	async fn synchronize(&self, mode: SyncMode) -> Result<SyncReport, EntityIngestionError>;
	async fn resume(&self, run: IngestionKey) -> Result<SyncReport, EntityIngestionError>;
}
```

These are signatures for discussion, not implemented Rust. Reuse DeclarationId, MemberId, IngestionKey, and existing errors. The domain model owns scope and completeness rules. The sync service owns orchestration. The Parliament adapter owns queries and external parsing. The artifact adapter owns immutable snapshot files. The existing load repository owns the atomic publication transaction and SQLx queries. Add versioned reversible migrations for checkpoint, generation, and run publication metadata when implementation is approved.

Model the Domain changes the design to explicit complete-capture and prepared-publication states. Make Operations Idempotent changes the publication protocol to atomic checkpoint advancement, exact-run replay, and expected-base checks.

## Limits and acceptance

Current noncompany identity strings contain the ingestion key. A complete re-resolution can therefore change funder IDs and URLs, as full refreshes already can. This proposal preserves matching semantics, not stable external identity IDs. Stable IDs require explicit cross-generation identity reconciliation and merge/split policy.

Neither a delta omission nor an empty member response authorizes deletion. Periodic full reconciliation reports omissions and catches updates missed by discovery. A future explicit retirement policy must remove projection records transactionally. Validate update coverage, indexing delay, and pagination behavior before treating the discovery checkpoint as a completeness guarantee.

Acceptance checks should compare baseline plus delta with a fresh full capture under the same evidence and policy. Compare semantic outputs rather than generation-specific IDs. Include parent-only updates, historical aliases, funding reorder, unknown/new members, empty scans, interrupted capture, load rollback, exact retry, and competing publication. Verify the real CLI, API search, and detail views after implementation.

## Synthesis

All three candidates converged on complete snapshots and global resolution. Candidate A is the base because it explicitly distinguishes discrepancies from deletions and defines replay ordering and all publication paths. Candidate B contributes changed-member acquisition and unchanged-content skipping. Candidate C contributes the explicit source-version ordering caution. Reject using filtered payloads as complete evidence, timestamp precision beyond source dates, and a mutable current filesystem pointer independent of the database commit. Fully incremental resolution remains an option when measured processing costs justify it.

The next implementation unit, after the user chooses an option, is sealed capture and transactional generation/checkpoint publication. No implementation is authorized in this turn.

Preserve former members already in the retained scope.

Observed API behavior makes hydration necessary. For interest 14513, an update-filtered list returned register 822 only. The same list endpoint filtered solely by InterestIds returned registers 822 and 794. The filtered response therefore cannot replace complete raw evidence. Probe responses are retained beside this document. This observation does not prove the behavior of every API query.

Merge reacquired records into immutable member partitions keyed by DeclarationId, checking member ownership. Retain old records missing from a response as discrepancies until withdrawal semantics are established. Snapshot manifests reference all member partitions, including reused immutable files. Record hashes, query policy, cohort, capture times, discovery receipts, and expected base generation. Materialize the complete snapshot for current stage readers. Do not relabel old evidence as freshly fetched. Compare canonical content separately from retrieval timestamps.

Only seal a capture after every planned member and page completes. Stage files under unique names and publish after closing and verifying them. Reject HTTP errors, inconsistent pagination, duplicate conflicting records, and truncated responses. Use bounded retries. Offset pagination has no documented transactional snapshot guarantee; overlap and periodic reconciliation reduce this risk but do not prove losslessness.

## Interpretation and publication

Run existing global clean and resolve over the complete merged snapshot. This retains parent evidence, reconsiders children whose parents changed, and derives company aliases from all surviving observations. Publish the complete resolved projection, because changed identity components can affect declarations outside the source delta.

Prepare durable immutable artifacts before the database transaction. Inside the existing declaration-loader lock, check the expected base generation, load the projection, rebuild groups, record the snapshot reference and fingerprints, and advance the discovery checkpoint in one transaction. An already committed run returns its recorded result before checking its old base. A stale base rejects publication and requires rebuilding against the current generation.

A crash before commit leaves the old checkpoint and projection. Resume can reuse sealed artifacts. A crash after commit returns the committed result. A successful empty scan advances coverage without replacing evidence or changing funder identities. Artifact retention pins every partition referenced by the committed snapshot. Production storage must survive scheduler replacement; the database projection cannot reconstruct complete source evidence.

```rust

struct DiscoveryWindow { /* checked inclusive source dates */ }
struct PublishedGeneration { /* generation, snapshot reference, coverage */ }
struct CompleteCapture { /* privately constructed from verified traversal */ }
struct PreparedPublication { /* expected base, run, snapshot, load fingerprint */ }
enum PublishOutcome { Committed(SyncReport), AlreadyCommitted(SyncReport), StaleBase }

impl DeclarationSyncService {
	async fn synchronize(&self, mode: SyncMode) -> Result<SyncReport, EntityIngestionError>;
	async fn resume(&self, run: IngestionKey) -> Result<SyncReport, EntityIngestionError>;
}
```

Model the Domain changes the design to explicit complete-capture and prepared-publication states. Make Operations Idempotent changes the publication protocol to atomic checkpoint advancement, exact-run replay, and expected-base checks.

## Limits and acceptance

Current noncompany identity strings contain the ingestion key. A complete re-resolution can therefore change funder IDs and URLs, as full refreshes already can. This proposal preserves matching semantics, not stable external identity IDs. Stable IDs require explicit cross-generation identity reconciliation and merge/split policy.

Neither a delta omission nor an empty member response authorizes deletion. Periodic full reconciliation reports omissions and catches updates missed by discovery. A future explicit retirement policy must remove projection records transactionally. Validate update coverage, indexing delay, and pagination behavior before treating the discovery checkpoint as a completeness guarantee.

Acceptance checks should compare baseline plus delta with a fresh full capture under the same evidence and policy. Compare semantic outputs rather than generation-specific IDs. Include parent-only updates, historical aliases, funding reorder, unknown/new members, empty scans, interrupted capture, load rollback, exact retry, and competing publication. Verify the real CLI, API search, and detail views after implementation.

All three candidates converged on complete snapshots and global resolution. Candidate A is the base because it explicitly distinguishes discrepancies from deletions and defines replay ordering and all publication paths. Candidate B contributes changed-member acquisition and unchanged-content skipping. Candidate C contributes the explicit source-version ordering caution. Reject using filtered payloads as complete evidence, timestamp precision beyond source dates, and a mutable current filesystem pointer independent of the database commit. Fully incremental resolution remains an option when measured processing costs justify it.

The next implementation unit, after the user chooses an option, is sealed capture and transactional generation/checkpoint publication. No implementation is authorized in this turn.

content.text:
I recommend **delta acquisition with a complete snapshot**, followed by the existing full cleaning, resolution, and loading pipeline. This reduces repeated downloads while preserving the evidence needed to interpret declarations correctly.

The options are:

| Option | Daily acquisition | Processing | Tradeoff |
|---|---|---|---|
| Full fetch with local diff | All declarations | Rebuild when content changes | Simplest change, but saves no API acquisition |
| **Fetch affected members** | Complete histories for members with changes | Full merged snapshot | Recommended starting point. Fits existing storage and preserves parent context |
| Fetch changed declarations | Complete records for changed IDs | Full merged snapshot | Less downloading, more record and relationship handling |
| Fully incremental pipeline | Changed declarations | Changed records and affected dependencies | Largest change. Requires persistent resolution evidence and identity merge/split handling |

The existing loader already replaces incoming declarations and preserves omitted declarations. The difficulty is upstream of loading. Resolution compares evidence across the run, and parent declarations can determine a child payment’s attribution. Loading a separately resolved daily delta could also replace a company’s historical aliases with only today’s aliases. See the [loader](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_loading.rs:560) and [parent attribution](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/attribution.rs:75).

Parliament documents inclusive `UpdatedFrom` and `PublishedFrom` filters. I would query both and combine the results. A live check also exposed an important detail. A date-filtered response returned one version of declaration 14513, while fetching that ID without date filters returned two. Filtered responses should therefore discover changes, then trigger an unfiltered fetch. The [official API specification](https://interests-api.parliament.uk/swagger/v2/swagger.json) documents the available filters.

The recommended daily flow is:

1. Read the last successfully published checkpoint. Choose a bounded date window with configurable overlap.
2. Discover affected members through publication and update queries. Include newly loaded members for a complete backfill.
3. Fetch those members’ complete declaration histories, including expired declarations.
4. Merge that evidence into a new immutable snapshot. Reuse unchanged member partitions and preserve their original capture times.
5. Clean and resolve the complete snapshot. This reconsiders unchanged children when a parent changes and preserves global funder evidence.
6. Publish the database projection, snapshot reference, and checkpoint in one transaction.

I would expose one scheduled operation:

```sh
exposed data declarations sync --config CONFIG
```

It would bootstrap with a full capture when needed. Explicit reconciliation and resume modes would support periodic full checks and recovery.

The domain model would distinguish a completed capture, a complete snapshot, and a prepared publication. The sync service would coordinate the existing services. The Parliament adapter would own discovery and pagination. Artifact storage would own immutable files and manifests. The existing load repository would own transactional publication.

Two principles shaped those choices. **Model the Domain** makes completeness an explicit checked state. **Make Operations Idempotent** puts checkpoint advancement inside publication and requires exact-run replay plus an expected-base check for competing runs.

Operationally, failed capture or processing leaves the published checkpoint unchanged. Resume reuses sealed artifacts. Empty or identical captures advance coverage without rebuilding resolution. Periodic full reconciliation catches discrepancies outside the discovery window. Missing records become reported discrepancies until upstream deletion semantics are established.

Two costs remain explicit:

- Cleaning, resolution, and grouping still process the complete corpus. We have not measured whether that fits the daily production budget.
- Noncompany funder IDs currently include the ingestion key. Full re-resolution can change IDs and URLs. Stable public identities require a separate cross-run identity design.

Three independent designs converged on this approach, and the independent comparison selected the affected-member version. The [full architecture sketch](/tmp/exposed-delta-architecture/design.md) includes signatures, ownership, recovery rules, and acceptance checks.

No repository files changed. My recommendation is the affected-member option first, with changed-declaration fetching as a later acquisition optimization.

# Revised candidate: declaration IDs, complete evidence

Recommend changed-declaration acquisition followed by complete-snapshot interpretation. The correction removes member refreshes and automatic member backfills from this workflow. `MemberId` supplies an existing lookup and scope boundary; member metadata has its own separately scheduled lifecycle.

## Caller experience

```sh
exposed data declarations sync --config CONFIG
exposed data declarations sync --config CONFIG --resume RUN_ID
exposed data declarations reconcile --config CONFIG
```

Daily sync operates on a committed declaration cohort and evidence baseline. Initial capture and deliberate cohort expansion belong to declaration reconciliation, using already stored member IDs. Neither command fetches or loads member metadata. Missing prerequisites produce an actionable error. New stored members do not silently expand established historical coverage; report them as awaiting declaration onboarding. Retain former members already in scope.

## Alternatives and decision

1. Full declaration capture and content diff: simplest acquisition, greatest remote work.
2. Changed-member full histories: viable fallback, fewer merge cases but refetches unrelated declarations whenever one changes. It need not update member metadata, but is broader than the daily requirement.
3. Changed declaration IDs plus complete-snapshot resolution: recommended. Hydrate changed IDs, preserve all other evidence, and reuse global interpretation.
4. Fully incremental resolution: defer; requires durable identity components, reverse dependencies, alias retention, and explicit identity merge/split rules.

The existing pipeline already interprets complete evidence globally. Incremental acquisition is a useful boundary without redesigning identity semantics.

## Acquisition contract

Freeze an inclusive source-date window with overlap and indexing lag. Union publication-filtered and update-filtered discovery results. Treat these payloads exclusively as ID discovery: observed filtered versions are truncated. Fetch each discovered ID unfiltered, including expired records and retaining all returned versions and source JSON. Registration dates are not correction timestamps.

Discovery may return records outside the cohort. Record their IDs, owners, and exclusion reason in the run receipt; they are explicitly outside coverage. For in-scope records, missing lookups, ownership conflicts, failed hydration, inconsistent pagination, and missing required parent evidence fail sealing. Never classify an error as an exclusion. Unknown ownership cannot be excluded until established. No member metadata retrieval is a recovery action.

Merge hydrated records into the complete immutable declaration-ID snapshot, indexed by owner and parent reference. Hydrate missing same-member parent declarations recursively, with cycle/conflict detection; preserve known parent evidence even when absent from discovery. Existing complete evidence remains available for unchanged children and global funder resolution. An omitted record or version is a discrepancy, never deletion evidence. Retain prior evidence pending an explicit source-supported retirement policy; conflicting versions require a documented selection rule, not arrival order.

Seal only after all required requests and dependency checks succeed. Manifest hashes, capture times, scope, query policy, base revision, and receipts make reused evidence distinguishable from fresh observations.

## Types and ownership

```rust
struct DeclarationCohort { /* explicit retained MemberIds */ }
struct DiscoveryWindow { /* checked source dates */ }
struct CompleteDeclarationSnapshot { /* verified records and dependencies */ }
struct PreparedPublication { /* run, expected revision, artifacts */ }
enum ScopeDecision { Included(MemberId), Excluded(ExclusionReason) }
enum PublishOutcome { Committed, AlreadyCommitted, StaleBase }

async fn synchronize(&self) -> Result<SyncReport, EntityIngestionError>;
async fn resume(&self, run: IngestionKey) -> Result<SyncReport, EntityIngestionError>;
async fn hydrate(&self, ids: DeclarationIds) -> Result<HydratedDeclarations, SourceError>;
```

Domain types own scope and completeness. The service orchestrates; Parliament parses external records; artifact storage owns durable snapshots; the existing loader owns transactional publication.

Run global clean/resolve and publish complete resolved evidence, retaining parent and alias context. Atomically commit projection, groups, artifact reference, and checkpoint under the existing loader lock with expected-revision protection. Check already-committed runs first. Empty successful scans advance revision and coverage without identity churn.

## Risks

Discovery is not a documented lossless changefeed; overlap and periodic declaration reconciliation mitigate omissions. Global resolution still costs work, and ingestion-derived noncompany IDs may change. Durable raw evidence remains essential. Verify baseline-plus-delta equivalence, parent-only corrections, out-of-scope receipts, in-scope failures, restart, and competing publication before rollout.

# Revised recommendation: changed declarations, complete interpretation

```sh
exposed data declarations sync --config CONFIG
exposed data declarations reconcile --config CONFIG
exposed data declarations sync --config CONFIG --resume RUN_ID
```

Daily sync discovers changed declaration IDs, hydrates those declarations without date filters, merges them into retained complete evidence, then runs global clean/resolve/load. Reconcile explicitly establishes or refreshes declaration history for the configured cohort. Neither command fetches or updates member metadata. Members remain a separately managed prerequisite.

## Options and decision

1. **Changed IDs plus complete snapshot — recommended.** Aligns acquisition with the daily declaration task. Requires keyed evidence merging and parent completeness, but avoids reacquiring entire member histories for an isolated correction.
2. **Changed-member declaration histories plus complete snapshot.** Still declarations-only when MemberId is merely a query key; a valid simpler acquisition adapter. It fetches unnecessary histories and is no longer the preferred conceptual boundary. It must not trigger member metadata loading or implicit cohort backfills.
3. **Fully incremental resolution.** Requires persistent identity observations, reverse dependencies, alias maintenance, and merge/split policy. Defer until measured global processing costs justify it.

## Ownership and invariants

A committed snapshot owns its explicit member cohort and complete retained declaration evidence. MemberId means ownership and eligibility, not a request to refresh a member. Initial capture and cohort expansion happen through explicit declaration reconciliation after the independent member update. Daily sync operates against the initialized cohort; newly available registry members do not silently enlarge it or trigger historical backfills. Report pending cohort additions.

Discovery unions inclusive publication/update windows, with overlap and indexing lag. Date-filtered responses are discovery only: observed source responses truncated version history. Hydrate discovered in-scope IDs through unfiltered InterestIds queries, including expired records and separate children. Preserve all returned versions and source JSON; use existing source-version selection semantics.

Classify records using explicit cohort membership. Persist out-of-cohort IDs and ownership as excluded discovery receipts. Missing ownership or inconsistent/conflicting ownership prevents reliable classification and fails capture. An in-scope declaration that cannot be hydrated, references an unavailable member prerequisite, or returns invalid data fails publication; never turn errors into exclusions.

Merge by DeclarationId into immutable snapshot partitions. Retain unchanged records and historical evidence. For every child, require its same-member parent evidence in the merged snapshot; hydrate a missing parent without date filters and repeat until closure. Missing or cross-member parents fail visibly. Changed parents are interpreted together with unchanged children. Preserve prior evidence when source records or versions disappear, recording discrepancies; omission is not withdrawal authorization. Explicitly conflicting versions require a documented replacement rule rather than timestamp guessing.

Global clean and resolution consume the entire merged snapshot, retaining noncompany identity observations and company aliases. Publish the entire resulting projection because changed identity components can affect unchanged declarations.

## Sketch and boundaries

```rust
enum DeclarationSyncMode { Daily, Reconcile }
struct DeclarationCohort { /* initialized eligible MemberIds */ }
struct CompleteDeclarationSnapshot { /* verified evidence + parent closure */ }
struct PreparedPublication { /* run, expected revision, snapshot, coverage */ }

impl DeclarationSyncService {
    async fn run(&self, mode: DeclarationSyncMode)
        -> Result<SyncReport, EntityIngestionError>;
    async fn resume(&self, run: IngestionKey)
        -> Result<SyncReport, EntityIngestionError>;
}
```

Domain types own scope and evidence completeness. The Parliament adapter owns discovery/hydration and external parsing. The artifact adapter owns immutable evidence and manifests. The existing loader owns projection, grouping, checkpoint, and publication revision in one locked transaction. Check exact committed-run replay before expected revision; stale runs rebuild. Durable sealed artifacts support restart. Empty scans advance coverage/revision without changing identity IDs.

## Remaining risks

Offset pagination and undocumented correction/deletion behavior prevent claiming a lossless changefeed. Periodic declaration reconciliation detects omissions. Global resolution retains existing ID churn across ingestion keys. Verify parent-only updates, historical aliases, explicit exclusions, in-scope failures, cohort expansion, empty scans, retries, rollback, and concurrent publication against equivalent complete evidence.

text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /tmp/exposed-delta-architecture/declarations-only-design.md <<'EOF'
# Declaration-only daily synchronization

This supersedes the earlier affected-member recommendation. It is a proposal, with no application implementation.

Member metadata has an independent, infrequent maintenance workflow. Daily synchronization reads existing MemberIds as ownership prerequisites. It never fetches member lists, refreshes metadata, loads members, or automatically adds historical member backfills.

## Options

| Option | Acquisition | Processing | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Full declaration acquisition with diff | All declarations | Full corpus on content change | Fallback. Saves no remote acquisition |
| Changed declaration IDs with complete snapshot | Changed records plus missing declaration context | Full corpus on content change | Recommended first version |
| Fully incremental interpretation | Changed records | Affected declarations and funder components | Larger design requiring persistent evidence and invalidation |

Refetching affected members' declaration histories is still a valid acquisition shortcut that does not require updating member metadata. It is broader than necessary and is not the recommended unit. Member-partitioned Parquet can remain an internal storage format.

## Caller experience

```sh
exposed data declarations sync --config CONFIG
exposed data declarations sync --config CONFIG --resume RUN_ID
exposed data declarations reconcile --config CONFIG
```

Sync discovers declaration changes, prepares complete evidence, interprets it, and atomically publishes. Resume continues sealed evidence for the same run. Reconcile bootstraps or periodically checks the complete declaration corpus for the existing scope. These commands do not update member metadata.

## Daily flow

1. Read the committed declaration snapshot, its explicit scope, publication revision, and discovery checkpoint. The scope records eligible existing MemberIds, including members with zero declarations. Require a verified baseline before advancing coverage.
2. Fix an inclusive source-date window with overlap and configurable indexing lag. Union publication-window and update-window results by DeclarationId. Treat filtered payloads as discovery only.
3. Hydrate in-scope IDs using unfiltered InterestIds requests, including expired records and preserving source JSON. Parse registrant MemberId at the API boundary and verify ownership. A live probe showed filtered interest 14513 had one version while its unfiltered response had two; do not store filtered payloads as complete replacements.
4. Replace each changed declaration's complete current raw record in a new immutable snapshot. Keep previous snapshots for audit. Retain unchanged declarations and their actual acquisition times. Rewrite affected local partitions as necessary, without refetching other declarations in those partitions. Content equality excludes acquisition time.
5. Resolve missing same-member parent context through declaration requests when needed. A transport or decode failure fails the run. Genuine unavailable parent evidence continues through existing unavailable-attribution rules. Do not convert cross-member parents into eligible parents or redefine existing domain behavior.
6. Run current global clean and resolve over the merged complete evidence. Publish the complete result because a parent or funder evidence change can affect unchanged declarations. Replace a hydrated declaration's funding entries as a complete set, allowing corrections and removed entries. Do not append individual funding rows.
7. Commit the projection, grouping, snapshot reference, run fingerprint, publication revision, and discovery checkpoint together through the existing loader transaction. Check expected revision to reject competing stale runs. Recognize committed retries before checking the old revision. Empty or content-identical runs advance checkpoint/revision without rebuilding resolution.

## Scope and recovery

Global discovery can find declarations outside the explicitly initialized scope. Record their IDs and owners as exclusions. Unknown ownership is a capture error, not an exclusion. An in-scope lookup or hydration failure blocks publication. Changing the member table does not silently grant historical declaration coverage. Deliberate scope expansion initializes the added declaration history before adopting it into daily coverage, without updating member metadata.

Every required request and page must complete before capture is sealed. Retain hashes and discovery receipts. Stage immutable artifacts durably before the database selects the new snapshot. Failed publication leaves old coverage and projection intact. Retain every artifact referenced by the committed snapshot. Do not use the newest filesystem directory as the committed base.

Date overlap and periodic declaration reconciliation mitigate discovery omissions. Neither guarantees a lossless changefeed. A missing declaration response is a discrepancy, not automatic retirement. Preserve old record evidence until the source's withdrawal contract and our retirement policy are established. A successful complete record response is authoritative for that declaration's current payload; never merge stale funding fields back into a correction. Earlier payloads remain in earlier immutable snapshots.

## Domain shape

```rust
enum DeclarationSyncMode { Daily, Reconcile }
struct DeclarationScope { /* eligible existing MemberIds and scope fingerprint */ }
struct DiscoveryWindow { /* checked inclusive source dates */ }
```

content.text:
**I recommend fetching changed declarations by ID, merging them into retained declaration evidence, then running the existing resolution pipeline.** Member maintenance stays entirely separate.

My previous proposal coupled the workflows unnecessarily. Members are existing ownership references for declarations. Their update frequency does not determine how declaration synchronization should work.

The revised options are:

| Option | Daily work | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Full declaration fetch with local diff | Download everything, detect differences | Simplest fallback, but repeats acquisition |
| **Declaration delta with full resolution** | Download changed declarations, resolve the complete retained corpus | Recommended first version |
| Fully incremental ingestion and resolution | Download and process only changes and affected dependencies | More complex. Requires persistent identity evidence and dependency tracking |

The recommended flow is:

1. **Discover changed declaration IDs.** Query publication and update windows since the last successful checkpoint, with overlap to accommodate inclusive dates and delayed publication.
2. **Fetch complete records for those IDs.** Use requests without date filters. The earlier live check showed that date-filtered responses can omit historical versions.
3. **Replace those declarations in a retained snapshot.** Keep unchanged declarations. Replace each changed declaration’s complete funding-entry set so corrections, removed entries, and reordered entries are handled correctly.
4. **Clean and resolve the complete snapshot.** This preserves historical funder aliases and lets a changed parent declaration affect an unchanged child.
5. **Publish atomically.** Commit the database changes, snapshot reference, and checkpoint together. Failed runs leave the previous published state intact.

The daily command would be:

```sh
exposed data declarations sync --config CONFIG
```

It would neither fetch member metadata nor update member records. Existing member IDs define the declaration scope. Records outside that scope would be reported explicitly. Expanding the scope later would require a deliberate declaration-history backfill through the separate reconciliation operation.

Fetching an affected member’s entire declaration history remains a possible implementation shortcut. However, I would now choose declaration IDs as the acquisition boundary. The existing files can remain partitioned by member without requiring those whole histories to be downloaded.

There is one reason I still recommend full resolution initially. **A small source delta does not necessarily produce a small interpretation delta.** A parent correction can change child attribution. New funder evidence can alter identities and aliases across declarations. Processing only today’s records would require redesigning those dependencies.

The domain model would make `DeclarationId` the merge key and `MemberId` an ownership reference. **Model the Domain** drove that separation. **Make Operations Idempotent** drove the checkpoint, retry, and atomic publication design.

The remaining limits are explicit. Global resolution still runs when evidence changes, and current run-scoped funder IDs can change. Whole declarations disappearing from the source also need a retirement policy; absence from a delta cannot mean deletion. Periodic full **declaration** reconciliation remains useful without refreshing members.

The [revised architecture sketch](/tmp/exposed-delta-architecture/declarations-only-design.md) includes boundaries, recovery rules, and verification cases. No application code or schema changed.

name: principle-prove-it-works
description: "Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'"
user-invocable: false

# Prove It Works

Verify every task output by checking the real thing directly. Do not infer from proxies, self-reports, or "it compiles."

**Why:** Unverified work has unknown correctness. Indirect verification (file mtimes, output freshness, agent self-reports, cached screenshots) feels cheaper than direct observation. Acting on a wrong inference costs far more than checking the source.

Check the real thing, not a proxy:
- Check process liveness directly, not indirectly through derived state
- Read the actual value, not a cached or derived representation
- When verification fails, suspect the observation method before suspecting the system

Verify the process as well as the outcome. A correct result can rest on a broken process, and a review that checks results passes it: a clause reconstructed from the user's paste instead of the durable record, a constraint honored by chance from a file never read. For each fact you relied on, name the record it came from and confirm that record is the one the project's rules point at.

Red is a colour, not a measurement. A failing check proves the instrument only when the failure content is the disagreement you predicted. An exception, an empty collection against a non-empty literal, and a real mismatch all print red, so quote the assertion's diff (`Extra items in the right set`), never the assertion (`assert {...} == {...}`). A convergence probe keys on behavior only the new artifact can produce, never an identity field the old one also emits. A same-SHA restart lets old code report the new commit SHA.

## Script the check when you can

The strongest proof is a deterministic script that re-runs the same comparison, not a one-time eyeball. Write the script, run it, and keep its output as an artifact a reviewer can re-run instead of trusting your word.

Keep the artifact visible for the human. Commit it only for large or complex work where the trail has to be auditable later, like a big port or migration (the **show-me-your-work** skill).

# Verify Exposed search

Run from the repository root. Read [the feature map](features/README.md).
The default strictness for this regression check is `0.8` for every search.
This check freezes search behavior over persisted identities. It does not rerun
declaration resolution or verify frontend rendering.

The five HTTP comparisons passed against the accepted development API. The
snapshot launch, doctor, and cleanup procedure has not yet been executed because
`exposed_search_regression` was absent. Treat that procedure as unverified until
the snapshot is available and the full run succeeds.

## Launch

Require Python 3, Cargo, and the existing Compose PostgreSQL service.
Check that the snapshot exists without changing it:

```sh
docker compose exec -T postgres psql -X -U exposed -d exposed_search_regression -c 'SELECT current_database()'
```

If the database is absent, report the missing prerequisite. The existing
`scripts/refresh-search-regression-db.sh` replaces the snapshot and requires
stopping source clients. Never refresh it as part of a regression run.

Build and start the current worktree's API with a read-only database connection:

```sh
export DATABASE_URL='REDACTED'
cargo build --package exposed --bin exposed
evidence_dir=$(mktemp -d /tmp/exposed-search-regression.XXXXXX)
./target/debug/exposed server >"$evidence_dir/server.log" 2>&1 &
server_pid=$!
```

Wait for `Listening on http://localhost:PORT` in `server.log` and a successful
HTTP response. Use that printed port. The server chooses an available port when
6999 is occupied. Do not reuse the already running development API.
Separate runs have their own processes, ports, and evidence directories and
share only the read-only snapshot. Do not run during a snapshot refresh.

## Doctor

Confirm the process is alive, its connection selects the snapshot, and its
printed port answers a real request:

```sh
kill -0 "$server_pid"
docker compose exec -T postgres psql -X -U exposed -d exposed_search_regression -c "SELECT datname, application_name, client_addr FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname = 'exposed_search_regression'"
cat "$evidence_dir/server.log"
curl --fail --get "$base_url/search" --data-urlencode 'term=unite' --data-urlencode 'strictness=0.8' --data-urlencode 'max_entries=10'
```

Set `base_url` to `http://127.0.0.1:PORT` using the startup log before the curl.
If startup fails, capture the log and clean up this run's process before retrying.

## Drive

Run the executable [HTTP check](../../../scripts/check-search-regression.py):

```sh
./scripts/check-search-regression.py "$base_url" "$evidence_dir/http"
```

Require five `PASS` lines and exit code 0. Cases and accepted results live in
`scripts/search-regression.json`. Keep the exact entity order, names,
match provenance, and recorded alias lists. The script has no baseline-update
mode. Investigate a diff before changing expectations.

## Populated funder groups

After changes to alias grouping or reviewed families, run the additional
`loaded_data_grouped_funders_regression` test. It starts the worktree's API and
checks BBC, GB News, and Premier League searches and detail pages against an
isolated copy of the 12 October 2026 development data. This database is separate
from `exposed_search_regression`. Apply the current migrations and run
`exposed data refresh-funder-groups` on the copy before the test. Do not change
the source database or refresh the frozen search snapshot during verification.

The preferred-name migration creates empty metadata; the refresh applies the
compiled reviewed-family names. Expect BBC, GB News, and Premier League in search
and detail names. Member declaration history continues to show recorded source
names.

Set `GROUPED_FUNDER_REGRESSION_DATABASE_URL` to a read-only URL for that copy.
The test also needs the same schema for SQLx compile-time query checks:

```sh
: "${GROUPED_FUNDER_REGRESSION_DATABASE_URL:?set a populated grouping database URL}"
DATABASE_URL="$GROUPED_FUNDER_REGRESSION_DATABASE_URL" \
  cargo test -p exposed --test integration loaded_data_grouped_funders_regression -- --ignored --exact
```

Require one passing test. It checks one result per search, the documented group
member and funding entry counts, recorded names, and both alias and reviewed
family link evidence. If the populated copy is unavailable, report that
prerequisite; the five-case search snapshot does not replace this check.

## Evidence

Retain `server.log` and the `http` directory under the printed `evidence_dir`.
Each case stores the GET URL, complete HTTP response, expected selected field,
and comparison diff. Search compares the entity array with IDs omitted. Funder detail compares the
funder profile with its ID omitted, including its recorded name and aliases.
Detail URLs use IDs from the current search response, never frozen IDs.
Funding totals are outside this check.

Use the real `/search` and `/funders/{UUID}` routes. Do not replace them with
mocks or direct database reads. Report failures with their diff and exit code.
The API connection is read-only and these routes only read stored data.

## Cleanup

```sh
kill "$server_pid"
wait "$server_pid" || true
test -s "$evidence_dir/server.log"
test -s "$evidence_dir/http/unite.response.json"
printf '%s\n' "$evidence_dir"
```

Kill only the process started by this run. Keep the snapshot and evidence.
Run cleanup after failed attempts too. If failure happened before HTTP capture,
retain the startup log and report the missing response evidence.

## Helpers

`scripts/check-search-regression.py BASE_URL NEW_EVIDENCE_DIRECTORY` needs only
Python's standard library. `--cases PATH` selects a different case file for a
temporary failure probe. It sends GET requests and never writes the database or
accepted baseline. Its evidence directory must not already exist.

# Rust domain development

Apply the [repository coding policy](../../../AGENTS.md). Choose the representation
that enforces the required behavior before adding implementation logic.

## Find the owner

Name the incoming data shape, the valid domain states, and the invariant the
change must preserve. Find the existing type that owns that rule. Search its
callers and serialized spellings before creating another representation.

Trace a changed domain type through its producer, encoder, decoder, service,
and persistence mapping. Change the affected consumers in the same task.

## Choose the representation

- Use an enum for a closed vocabulary. Share its serialization and deserialization
  definition across producers and consumers. When a separately versioned external
  contract needs its own type, convert it explicitly into the canonical domain
  type at the boundary.
- Represent mutually exclusive states with an enum carrying the fields each
  state requires. Use newtypes for identifiers with different meanings and
  checked constructors for values whose validity depends on runtime facts.
- Use exhaustive matches without a fallback when variants require different
  behavior. Adding a variant must require a decision at those matches. Do not
  add artificial matches when every variant already supports the same operation.
- Keep transport DTOs only where the external shape differs from the domain
  shape. Their domain-bearing fields still use the canonical types. Reuse an
  existing result record when it already defines the serialized contract.

## Parse at the boundary

Decode external values into domain types before passing them to services.
Reject unknown labels during parsing. Do not parse a domain enum into a string
and then reconstruct its vocabulary with a membership check.

Keep checks for runtime facts such as duplicate IDs, missing references,
artifact digests, and stored timestamps at the responsible boundary. Types
cannot establish facts about files or database rows that have not been read.
Propagate the existing error types instead of hiding failures with defaults.

Keep domain decisions in the domain model and transaction ownership in the
repository. Convert typed values into storage representations at the persistence
boundary using the canonical encoding. Preserve existing service abstractions.

## Fix the structure

When a failure reveals two owners for one rule, identify the canonical owner and
delete the competing definition. Updating both copies leaves the cause intact.
Stay within the affected contract rather than expanding into unrelated cleanup.

In Exposed, the resolution domain owns `IdentityBasis`, `PairReason`, and the
attribution decision types in
[`declaration_resolution.rs`](../../../exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution.rs).
The [declaration loader](../../../exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_loading.rs)
must decode those types. It must not maintain a second list of accepted labels.
This applies to other finite domain vocabularies too.

## Verify the contract

Run the relevant behavior checks and the real entry point affected by the change.
For serialized contracts, verify that producer output is readable by the consumer
and that malformed external values are rejected. Preserve the intended wire
format, supported versions, and persistence behavior unless the task changes them.

Check the compiler guarantee directly when the task relies on it. For example,
temporarily add a variant to confirm the semantic matches reject missing handling,
then revert the probe. A passing runtime test does not prove exhaustiveness.

Run formatting and applicable compiler or lint checks. Distinguish diagnostics
introduced by the change from existing failures. Report which invalid state the
types now exclude and which runtime checks remain necessary.

stopping source clients. Never refresh it as part of a regression run.

Build and start the current worktree's API with a read-only database connection:

```sh
export DATABASE_URL='REDACTED'
cargo build --package exposed --bin exposed
evidence_dir=$(mktemp -d /tmp/exposed-search-regression.XXXXXX)
./target/debug/exposed server >"$evidence_dir/server.log" 2>&1 &
server_pid=$!
```

Wait for `Listening on http://localhost:PORT` in `server.log` and a successful
HTTP response. Use that printed port. The server chooses an available port when
6999 is occupied. Do not reuse the already running development API.
Separate runs have their own processes, ports, and evidence directories and
share only the read-only snapshot. Do not run during a snapshot refresh.

## Doctor

Confirm the process is alive, its connection selects the snapshot, and its
printed port answers a real request:

```sh
kill -0 "$server_pid"
docker compose exec -T postgres psql -X -U exposed -d exposed_search_regression -c "SELECT datname, application_name, client_addr FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname = 'exposed_search_regression'"
cat "$evidence_dir/server.log"
curl --fail --get "$base_url/search" --data-urlencode 'term=unite' --data-urlencode 'strictness=0.8' --data-urlencode 'max_entries=10'
```

Set `base_url` to `http://127.0.0.1:PORT` using the startup log before the curl.
If startup fails, capture the log and clean up this run's process before retrying.

## Drive

Run the executable [HTTP check](../../../scripts/check-search-regression.py):

```sh
./scripts/check-search-regression.py "$base_url" "$evidence_dir/http"
```

Require five `PASS` lines and exit code 0. Cases and accepted results live in
`scripts/search-regression.json`. Keep the exact entity order, names,
match provenance, and recorded alias lists. The script has no baseline-update
mode. Investigate a diff before changing expectations.

## Populated funder groups

After changes to alias grouping or reviewed families, run the additional
`loaded_data_grouped_funders_regression` test. It starts the worktree's API and
checks BBC, GB News, and Premier League searches and detail pages against an
isolated copy of the 12 October 2026 development data. This database is separate
from `exposed_search_regression`. Apply the current migrations and run
`exposed data refresh-funder-groups` on the copy before the test. Do not change
the source database or refresh the frozen search snapshot during verification.

The preferred-name migration creates empty metadata; the refresh applies the
compiled reviewed-family names. Expect BBC, GB News, and Premier League in search
and detail names. Member declaration history continues to show recorded source
names.

Set `GROUPED_FUNDER_REGRESSION_DATABASE_URL` to a read-only URL for that copy.
The test also needs the same schema for SQLx compile-time query checks:

```sh
: "${GROUPED_FUNDER_REGRESSION_DATABASE_URL:?set a populated grouping database URL}"
DATABASE_URL="$GROUPED_FUNDER_REGRESSION_DATABASE_URL" \
  cargo test -p exposed --test integration loaded_data_grouped_funders_regression -- --ignored --exact
```

Require one passing test. It checks one result per search, the documented group
member and funding entry counts, recorded names, and both alias and reviewed
family link evidence. If the populated copy is unavailable, report that
prerequisite; the five-case search snapshot does not replace this check.

## Evidence

Retain `server.log` and the `http` directory under the printed `evidence_dir`.
Each case stores the GET URL, complete HTTP response, expected selected field,
and comparison diff. Search compares the entity array with IDs omitted. Funder detail compares the
funder profile with its ID omitted, including its recorded name and aliases.
Detail URLs use IDs from the current search response, never frozen IDs.
Funding totals are outside this check.

Use the real `/search` and `/funders/{UUID}` routes. Do not replace them with
mocks or direct database reads. Report failures with their diff and exit code.
The API connection is read-only and these routes only read stored data.

## Cleanup

```sh
kill "$server_pid"
wait "$server_pid" || true
test -s "$evidence_dir/server.log"
test -s "$evidence_dir/http/unite.response.json"
printf '%s\n' "$evidence_dir"
```

Kill only the process started by this run. Keep the snapshot and evidence.
Run cleanup after failed attempts too. If failure happened before HTTP capture,
retain the startup log and report the missing response evidence.

## Helpers

`scripts/check-search-regression.py BASE_URL NEW_EVIDENCE_DIRECTORY` needs only
Python's standard library. `--cases PATH` selects a different case file for a
temporary failure probe. It sends GET requests and never writes the database or
accepted baseline. Its evidence directory must not already exist.

name: rust-domain-development
description: "Design and change Rust domain types, service boundaries, and serialized contracts in Exposed. Use for Rust features, bug fixes, and refactors that touch those concerns."
---

# Rust domain development

Apply the [repository coding policy](../../../AGENTS.md). Choose the representation
that enforces the required behavior before adding implementation logic.

## Find the owner

Name the incoming data shape, the valid domain states, and the invariant the
change must preserve. Find the existing type that owns that rule. Search its
callers and serialized spellings before creating another representation.

Trace a changed domain type through its producer, encoder, decoder, service,
and persistence mapping. Change the affected consumers in the same task.

## Choose the representation

- Use an enum for a closed vocabulary. Share its serialization and deserialization
  definition across producers and consumers. When a separately versioned external
  contract needs its own type, convert it explicitly into the canonical domain
  type at the boundary.
- Represent mutually exclusive states with an enum carrying the fields each
  state requires. Use newtypes for identifiers with different meanings and
  checked constructors for values whose validity depends on runtime facts.
- Use exhaustive matches without a fallback when variants require different
  behavior. Adding a variant must require a decision at those matches. Do not
  add artificial matches when every variant already supports the same operation.
- Keep transport DTOs only where the external shape differs from the domain
  shape. Their domain-bearing fields still use the canonical types. Reuse an
  existing result record when it already defines the serialized contract.

## Parse at the boundary

Decode external values into domain types before passing them to services.
Reject unknown labels during parsing. Do not parse a domain enum into a string
and then reconstruct its vocabulary with a membership check.

Keep checks for runtime facts such as duplicate IDs, missing references,
artifact digests, and stored timestamps at the responsible boundary. Types
cannot establish facts about files or database rows that have not been read.
Propagate the existing error types instead of hiding failures with defaults.

Keep domain decisions in the domain model and transaction ownership in the
repository. Convert typed values into storage representations at the persistence
boundary using the canonical encoding. Preserve existing service abstractions.

## Fix the structure

When a failure reveals two owners for one rule, identify the canonical owner and
delete the competing definition. Updating both copies leaves the cause intact.
Stay within the affected contract rather than expanding into unrelated cleanup.

In Exposed, the resolution domain owns `IdentityBasis`, `PairReason`, and the
attribution decision types in
[`declaration_resolution.rs`](../../../exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution.rs).
The [declaration loader](../../../exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_loading.rs)
must decode those types. It must not maintain a second list of accepted labels.
This applies to other finite domain vocabularies too.

## Verify the contract

Run the relevant behavior checks and the real entry point affected by the change.
For serialized contracts, verify that producer output is readable by the consumer
and that malformed external values are rejected. Preserve the intended wire
format, supported versions, and persistence behavior unless the task changes them.

Check the compiler guarantee directly when the task relies on it. For example,
temporarily add a variant to confirm the semantic matches reject missing handling,
then revert the probe. A passing runtime test does not prove exhaustiveness.

Run formatting and applicable compiler or lint checks. Distinguish diagnostics
introduced by the change from existing failures. Report which invalid state the
types now exclude and which runtime checks remain necessary.
"}

name: show-me-your-work
description: "Keep a reviewable decision trail for long-running or unattended work: a TSV log with one row per decision (what, why, evidence, result). Local by default; commit it when a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result. Use for /show-me-your-work, autonomous or multi-phase runs, or work a human reviews after stepping away."
---

# Show me your work

On GitHub Copilot, read the [platform mapping](../poteto-mode/references/copilot-tools.md), including its per-skill notes, before following this skill.

Keep one canonical log.

## The format

A single TSV file, one row per decision. Cells stay single-line. Evidence is a pointer, not prose.

Copy `references/decision-log-template.tsv` (the header row) to start a clean log. Columns:

- **ts.** ISO8601 timestamp.
- **phase.** The phase or workstream.
- **decision.** What was chosen or done, one line.
- **why.** The reason in plain words. If a principle drove it, say it plainly, not as a jargon tag.
- **evidence.** A link or path that proves it: commit SHA, PR number, `file:line`, or an artifact, trace, or screenshot path. Never a paragraph.
- **result.** The outcome or predicate state: `tests green`, `reverted`, `pixel-diff 0`, `INCONCLUSIVE`, `open`.

An example, plain-spoken so a reviewer reads it at a glance.

```
ts	phase	decision	why	evidence	result
2026-05-24T09:02:00Z	frame	counted the work first, about 100 components and roughly 75 hours	wanted to know the size before starting a long run	commit 3a9f1c2	found 5 things to sort out before starting
2026-05-24T09:40:00Z	harness	took screenshots of the old version before changing anything	so we can compare old against new and catch any visual change	scripts/snapshot.sh, baseline/	saved 120 reference screenshots
2026-05-24T11:15:00Z	widget	moved the widget styles over without changing how it looks	keep the change small and the result identical	commit 7c21e0a, pixel-diff 0	looks identical, tests pass
2026-05-24T12:30:00Z	widget	threw out a helper's work because its screenshots were blank	checked the real files instead of trusting its summary	worktree reset	reverted, tightened the instructions for next time
```

## Logging a row

Write each entry the way you'd tell a teammate what you did. Plain words, concrete actions, no AI speak or abstract jargon (the **unslop** skill applies to log text too).

Use the helper `scripts/log.sh <logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>`. It stamps `ts`, writes the header on first use, strips stray tabs/newlines, and prefixes any cell starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, or `"` with a single quote. A bare `printf` appending a row works too, but mind those same bytes if cells come from generated or user-supplied text.

Log decision points and checkpoints, not every action: a fork chosen, a unit completed with its verification result, a pivot or revert with its trigger, a blocker surfaced, a gate fixed. For loop runs, one row per iteration. Skip the trivial and self-evident.

A run is one agent conversation, including its later turns and any summary of it. A pickup, a replacement agent, or a new chat starts a new run. When a run adds to a log that already has rows, its first row has phase `start`, and so does its first row after another run's `start` row. So a run that comes back to a log in a later turn first reads the log's last rows to see whether another run wrote since. A `start` row names the `ts` range of the rows before it that this run did not write, and its evidence names this run, such as its agent id. Use phase `start` for nothing else.

## Where it lives

By default the log is a working artifact, not committed. Keep it at `decisions.tsv` in the work dir, or `.audit/<task-slug>.tsv` when several efforts run at once, and leave it out of git.

Commit it only when the work is ambitious enough that a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result.

## Rules

- Append-only. A wrong call gets a new row that supersedes it. Never edit or delete history.
- Prefer evidence produced by committed scripts over hand-made one-offs (the **encode-lessons-in-structure** principle skill).

## Audit the log against the transcript

At the end of the run, before handing back, check the log told the truth. Read this run's transcript under Claude Code's per-project transcripts directory at `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/`. Don't glob across `~/.claude/projects/`. That reads unrelated private chats. Walk this run's rows against what actually happened. Each stretch of them begins at one of this run's `start` rows, or at the first row if this run created the log, and ends at the next `start` row of another run:

- Check that every row maps to a real decision or action.
- Check that each row's evidence resolves and shows what the row claims.
- A fork, pivot, or abandoned approach that shaped the work but isn't logged is a gap. Add it.

Correct the log, not the story. The audit never edits or removes a row, even an invented one. When a row records neither a real decision nor a real action, or its claim or evidence is wrong, add a row that supersedes it with what actually happened and a pointer that resolves. This audit does not check rows outside this run's stretches. If this run's own work shows one of them is wrong, supersede it like any wrong call.

## Cross-model review of the trail

Before handing back, spawn a subagent on a different model family from the one that did the work. Self-review is not a substitute. The subagent reads the audit trail and the run's transcript, then flags what the user should pay attention to. Not a redo of the work, a scan for what's suboptimal or risky.

- Decisions logged with weak or absent evidence.
- Verification steps skipped or claimed without proof in the transcript.
- Choices that look risky in hindsight (premature, scope-creeping, papering over a symptom).
- Gaps the user would otherwise miss on a casual skim.

Every reply for a run that produced a trail ends with an "Attention" section. Lead with the reviewer's model on its own line (`reviewed by <model>`), then list each flag pointing to specific rows or moments. "No flags" is a valid value. The model name is not.

## Reviewing the trail

Read top to bottom, follow the evidence pointers, spot-check. GitHub renders a committed TSV as a table. `column -s$'\t' -t decisions.tsv` renders it in a terminal.

## Composing this skill

Other skills route their audit trail here instead of inventing one. Reference it by name and let it own the format. Don't restate the columns.
### Opening a PR

Invoked at the end of every other playbook.

**Worktree.** Work from a git worktree off main. Subagents inherit it. Multiple `Agent` calls on the same branch each get their own worktree, or `git fetch && git reset --hard origin/<branch>` between them. Dirty branch with unrelated work: patch out, fresh worktree, apply. Snarled worktree: reset from main, redo minimally. Before you commit, merge, or deploy from a worktree, list the live agents and stop every one that holds it, including grandchildren you never launched. A delegate's children do not inherit its brief, so a read-only instruction never reaches them. Confirm each stop, then run `git status` and read the tree you are about to ship.

**Commits.** Commit liberally. Rebase into small, ordered commits before opening PRs. Each commit is a future PR: landable, ordered to tell the story. Amend when the fix belongs in a just-made commit. New commit when separable.

**PRs.** Run `/deslop` over the diff before commit. Run `/no-comments` before review. Write every PR title, PR description, and commit body with `/technical-writing`, then apply `/unslop`. Apply every technical-writing layer except Diátaxis. Use one word for each action, keep articles, and avoid `-ing` when a plain verb works.

**Titles.** Use Conventional Commits in the form `type(scope): subject`. Use `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`, or `perf` as the type. Use the changed area, such as `pstack` or `poteto-mode`, as the scope. Keep the subject short and imperative. Name a real symbol when one carries the change. For example, `fix(pstack): retarget opening-a-pr babysit trigger`. Do not add a trailing period.

**Descriptions.** The PR body is a briefing, not the lab notebook. A reviewer who has the diff should learn why the change exists, what it leaves out, what it could break, and how you proved it works, in under a minute. Write short, simple sentences with few identifiers. Do not write walls of text. The squash commit body is the PR body. If the body would make the squash commit longer than about 40 lines, cut the body.

Put each section under a `##` heading, not a bold lead-in, so the sections stand apart. Use these sections in order. Drop a section when it has nothing to say.

- `## Why` gives the problem and the approach in one to three short sentences. Do not list SHAs or rebase genealogy. Do not add a "based on main" preamble.
- `## What changed` has one to three short bullets. Name a real symbol or path only when it carries the change. Name both sides of a rename or retarget.
- `## Scope` always names what the PR covers and what it deliberately leaves out, for example a related follow-up or a known gap. Use one to three short items. Do not list symbols or paths, and do not write a file-by-file essay.
- `## Tradeoffs` names only rejected alternatives that a reviewer would otherwise ask about. Skip this section when there was no real choice.
- `## Blast Radius` gives one or two sentences on who or what the change touches and why that is safe or risky. If main is red, state the cost of leaving it red.
- `## Verification` has one to three bullets. Each bullet names a real run path and its outcome. For a performance change, report one primary number with its unit in `before → after` form. Link the arena or swarm directory for the remaining evidence. Do not include sample-size methodology, swarm recitals, or metric tables.

After these sections, attach videos or screenshots when they prove a claim. Do not paste full SHAs, swarm or arena lane recitals, lever-correction essays, file-by-file checklists, or "CLEAN" verdicts. Put these details in a linked artifact. A commit body does not restate its subject.

**Forge.** Resolve the forge before the first PR operation and keep that choice for create, edit, view, watch, and merge. GitHub CLI (`gh`) is the default. If `command -v origin` succeeds and Origin can resolve the repository, prefer `origin pr ...`. If Origin is absent or cannot resolve the repository, stay on `gh` and record the fallback. Do not require Graphite (`gt`).

**Built-in PR tool.** When the run provides a built-in PR tool, create, edit, retarget, and mark ready through it, never through a forge CLI. Its own instructions say how. A PR made with the CLI misses what the tool tracks, such as a description later runs can edit. Use the resolved forge for everything the tool does not cover, and for every PR operation when the run has no such tool.

**Size and stacks.** Prefer five narrow PRs to one large PR. A stack is a base-branch chain. The root PR targets trunk. Each child branch rebases onto its parent's exact tip and its PR targets the parent branch. Without a built-in PR tool, create a child with `origin pr create --status open --base <parent-branch>` or `gh pr create --base <parent-branch>` according to the resolved forge, and retarget an existing child with `origin pr edit <pr> --base <parent-branch>` or `gh pr edit <pr> --base <parent-branch>`. Branch from trunk only for independent work. Rebase on trunk before substantial stack work.

**Readiness.** Open every PR ready, never as a draft. A built-in PR tool can default to draft, so set `draft: false` on every creation call through it. With Origin, pass `--status open`. With `gh`, omit `--draft`. If a PR still opens as a draft, mark it ready through the PR tool, or run `origin pr ready <number>` or `gh pr ready <number>` according to the resolved forge. Run `origin pr view <number>` or `gh pr view <number>` before you refer to PR status.

**Babysit.** Opening a PR does not start a babysit. Post the URL and keep building. Finish the phase or stack first. Run a separate babysit pass only when the user asks for one after the whole stack exists, per `babysit.md`. A babysit for each new PR stalls the build and spends checks on commits that later waves restart. Push back when feedback drifts from intent.

A subagent that opens a PR runs `interrogate`, `/deslop`, and `/no-comments`, and posts the URL. Then it returns to the parent without babysitting, unless it is an Autopilot-full or Autopilot-stack owner. That owner's brief assigns the babysit loop and is the ask `playbooks/babysit.md` waits for. The owner starts the loop after its code-ready report and reports merge-ready or STACK-READY as its playbook says. The rules here and in `playbooks/babysit.md` that hold babysitting until a whole stack is built do not apply to that owner.

Every reply for a run that produced a trail ends with an "Attention" section. Lead with the reviewer's model on its own line (`reviewed by <model>`), then list each flag pointing to specific rows or moments. "No flags" is a valid value. The model name is not.

## Reviewing the trail

Read top to bottom, follow the evidence pointers, spot-check. GitHub renders a committed TSV as a table. `column -s$'\t' -t decisions.tsv` renders it in a terminal.

## Composing this skill

Other skills route their audit trail here instead of inventing one. Reference it by name and let it own the format. Don't restate the columns.
### Opening a PR

Invoked at the end of every other playbook.

**Worktree.** Work from a git worktree off main. Subagents inherit it. Multiple `Agent` calls on the same branch each get their own worktree, or `git fetch && git reset --hard origin/<branch>` between them. Dirty branch with unrelated work: patch out, fresh worktree, apply. Snarled worktree: reset from main, redo minimally. Before you commit, merge, or deploy from a worktree, list the live agents and stop every one that holds it, including grandchildren you never launched. A delegate's children do not inherit its brief, so a read-only instruction never reaches them. Confirm each stop, then run `git status` and read the tree you are about to ship.

**Commits.** Commit liberally. Rebase into small, ordered commits before opening PRs. Each commit is a future PR: landable, ordered to tell the story. Amend when the fix belongs in a just-made commit. New commit when separable.

**PRs.** Run `/deslop` over the diff before commit. Run `/no-comments` before review. Write every PR title, PR description, and commit body with `/technical-writing`, then apply `/unslop`. Apply every technical-writing layer except Diátaxis. Use one word for each action, keep articles, and avoid `-ing` when a plain verb works.

**Titles.** Use Conventional Commits in the form `type(scope): subject`. Use `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`, or `perf` as the type. Use the changed area, such as `pstack` or `poteto-mode`, as the scope. Keep the subject short and imperative. Name a real symbol when one carries the change. For example, `fix(pstack): retarget opening-a-pr babysit trigger`. Do not add a trailing period.

**Descriptions.** The PR body is a briefing, not the lab notebook. A reviewer who has the diff should learn why the change exists, what it leaves out, what it could break, and how you proved it works, in under a minute. Write short, simple sentences with few identifiers. Do not write walls of text. The squash commit body is the PR body. If the body would make the squash commit longer than about 40 lines, cut the body.

Put each section under a `##` heading, not a bold lead-in, so the sections stand apart. Use these sections in order. Drop a section when it has nothing to say.

- `## Why` gives the problem and the approach in one to three short sentences. Do not list SHAs or rebase genealogy. Do not add a "based on main" preamble.
- `## What changed` has one to three short bullets. Name a real symbol or path only when it carries the change. Name both sides of a rename or retarget.
- `## Scope` always names what the PR covers and what it deliberately leaves out, for example a related follow-up or a known gap. Use one to three short items. Do not list symbols or paths, and do not write a file-by-file essay.
- `## Tradeoffs` names only rejected alternatives that a reviewer would otherwise ask about. Skip this section when there was no real choice.
- `## Blast Radius` gives one or two sentences on who or what the change touches and why that is safe or risky. If main is red, state the cost of leaving it red.
- `## Verification` has one to three bullets. Each bullet names a real run path and its outcome. For a performance change, report one primary number with its unit in `before → after` form. Link the arena or swarm directory for the remaining evidence. Do not include sample-size methodology, swarm recitals, or metric tables.

After these sections, attach videos or screenshots when they prove a claim. Do not paste full SHAs, swarm or arena lane recitals, lever-correction essays, file-by-file checklists, or "CLEAN" verdicts. Put these details in a linked artifact. A commit body does not restate its subject.

**Forge.** Resolve the forge before the first PR operation and keep that choice for create, edit, view, watch, and merge. GitHub CLI (`gh`) is the default. If `command -v origin` succeeds and Origin can resolve the repository, prefer `origin pr ...`. If Origin is absent or cannot resolve the repository, stay on `gh` and record the fallback. Do not require Graphite (`gt`).

**Built-in PR tool.** When the run provides a built-in PR tool, create, edit, retarget, and mark ready through it, never through a forge CLI. Its own instructions say how. A PR made with the CLI misses what the tool tracks, such as a description later runs can edit. Use the resolved forge for everything the tool does not cover, and for every PR operation when the run has no such tool.

**Size and stacks.** Prefer five narrow PRs to one large PR. A stack is a base-branch chain. The root PR targets trunk. Each child branch rebases onto its parent's exact tip and its PR targets the parent branch. Without a built-in PR tool, create a child with `origin pr create --status open --base <parent-branch>` or `gh pr create --base <parent-branch>` according to the resolved forge, and retarget an existing child with `origin pr edit <pr> --base <parent-branch>` or `gh pr edit <pr> --base <parent-branch>`. Branch from trunk only for independent work. Rebase on trunk before substantial stack work.

**Readiness.** Open every PR ready, never as a draft. A built-in PR tool can default to draft, so set `draft: false` on every creation call through it. With Origin, pass `--status open`. With `gh`, omit `--draft`. If a PR still opens as a draft, mark it ready through the PR tool, or run `origin pr ready <number>` or `gh pr ready <number>` according to the resolved forge. Run `origin pr view <number>` or `gh pr view <number>` before you refer to PR status.

**Babysit.** Opening a PR does not start a babysit. Post the URL and keep building. Finish the phase or stack first. Run a separate babysit pass only when the user asks for one after the whole stack exists, per `babysit.md`. A babysit for each new PR stalls the build and spends checks on commits that later waves restart. Push back when feedback drifts from intent.

A subagent that opens a PR runs `interrogate`, `/deslop`, and `/no-comments`, and posts the URL. Then it returns to the parent without babysitting, unless it is an Autopilot-full or Autopilot-stack owner. That owner's brief assigns the babysit loop and is the ask `playbooks/babysit.md` waits for. The owner starts the loop after its code-ready report and reports merge-ready or STACK-READY as its playbook says. The rules here and in `playbooks/babysit.md` that hold babysitting until a whole stack is built do not apply to that owner.
